title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 87
paragraphs: Darius, having gazed on the Pontus, sailed back to the bridge, of which Mandrocles a Samian had been chief constructor. Having gazed on the Bosphorus as well, he set up beside it two pillars of white stone with characters cut upon them—on one Assyrian, on the other Hellenic—giving the names of all the nations he was leading with him; and he was leading all over whom he ruled. The whole number of them, without the naval force, was reckoned at seventy myriads including cavalry; and ships had been gathered together to the number of six hundred. These pillars the Byzantians later conveyed to their city, after the events of which I speak, and used them for the altar of Artemis Orthosia, except for one stone which was left standing beside the temple of Dionysos in Byzantion, covered with Assyrian characters. Now the place on the Bosphorus where Darius made his bridge is, as I conclude, midway between Byzantion and the temple at the mouth of the Pontus.
